slides.title: Dial 15100
slides.body: NALSA runs a toll-free legal aid helpline, 15100, for guidance and free legal services across India.

slides.body: Under Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act: women, children, SC/ST, persons with disabilities, industrial workers, people in custody and low-income persons.

Can't afford a lawyer? Free legal aid is your legal right in India. ⚖️

📞 Call NALSA's toll-free legal aid helpline: 15100
👩‍👧 Eligible under Section 12, Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987: women, children, SC/ST, persons with disabilities, industrial workers, people in custody, disaster victims and low-income persons
🏛️ Apply on plain paper at the District Legal Services Authority (in the district court) or Taluk/Sub-divisional Legal Services Committee
💻 You can also apply online on the NALSA legal services portal
🤝 Lok Adalat: no court fee when a matter is filed there

caption_linkedin:
Access to justice should not depend on the ability to pay. Article 39A of the Constitution and the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 make free legal aid a right for eligible people in India.

• NALSA operates a toll-free legal aid helpline: 15100
• Eligible under Section 12: women, children, members of SC/ST, persons with disabilities, victims of trafficking or disasters, industrial workers, persons in custody, and persons below the prescribed income limit
• Applications can be made on plain paper to the District Legal Services Authority, Taluk/Sub-divisional Legal Services Committee, High Court or Supreme Court Legal Services Committee — or online via the NALSA portal
• Free legal services can include representation by a panel advocate and certified copies of orders and documents
• No court fee is payable when a matter is filed in a Lok Adalat

To learn how secure online consultations with Bar Council-verified advocates work, visit https://advocatesetu.com
